title: Calendar Event
story: Your calendar app shows events � meetings, birthdays, holidays, and deadlines. Each event has a date and a type. Holidays have a name ("Christmas"), but meetings don't need one. You need a system that handles all event types uniformly.
why: A struct for dates plus an enum for event types gives you a flexible calendar that formats any event.
analogy: A calendar event is like a sticky note. The date is the day you stick it on. The event type is the color of the note � red for deadlines, green for birthdays. Holidays get an extra label written on them.
try_it: Add `Appointment(with: Str)` to EventType. It carries the name of the person you're meeting. Add your actual birthday as an event. Add a doctor's appointment for next week. Format and print both events.
tips: Put the date struct first � it's used by Event, so it must be defined above
Match on `e.kind` to handle each event type differently in your format function
Use `Int` for date components � years, months, and days are whole numbers
common_mistakes: Defining Event before Date � the compiler reads top-to-bottom and won't know what Date is
Mixing up the order when creating a Date: `Date{ day: 25; month: 12; year: 2026; }` is correct
